# Disagreement Log — Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 1

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Chapter:** POX 1 — Joachim's humiliation and desert fast

---

## Disagreements

**1. 1:1 — "In the histories" vs. "In the records"**
- EMET: "In the histories of the twelve tribes"
- LOGOS: "In the records of the twelve tribes"
- PNEUMA: "The ancient records of the twelve tribes"
- Note: Greek *historiais* can mean either histories/chronicles or records. LOGOS/SOPHIA prefer "records" for archival precision; EMET preserves "histories" for narrative sense.

**2. 1:1 — Rendering of the self-reasoning about gifts**
- EMET: preserves the tripartite structure ("abundance…for all…my gift…my repentance")
- LOGOS: restructures into two clauses for clarity
- PNEUMA: paraphrases freely ("This is how I will make things right before God")
- Note: The Greek is a complex internal monologue. EMET preserves the three-clause parallelism; PNEUMA loses the repentance/atonement distinction.

**3. 1:2 — "Reuben" as the challenger**
- All three agents preserve Reuben as the name. Note: Some MSS omit the name or give other names. P.Bodmer V has Reuben.

**4. 1:2 — "you have not made seed in Israel"**
- EMET: "you have not made seed in Israel" (literal)
- LOGOS: "you have produced no offspring in Israel"
- PNEUMA: "you've never fathered a child in Israel"
- Note: Greek *ou epoiesas sperma* is literally "you have not made seed." EMET preserves the biological directness; PNEUMA modernizes.

**5. 1:3 — "the records of the twelve tribes"**
- EMET/LOGOS: "records of the twelve tribes"
- PNEUMA: "genealogical archives"
- Note: PNEUMA's addition of "genealogical" is interpretive but accurate; not in the Greek.

**6. 1:3 — Extent of Joachim's research**
- EMET: "all the righteous had raised up seed"
- LOGOS: "every righteous man had indeed produced offspring"
- PNEUMA: "every righteous man had indeed fathered offspring" + adds "He pored over the lists"
- Note: "Pored over the lists" is a PNEUMA addition with no Greek basis.

**7. 1:4 — "did not appear to his wife" vs. other renderings**
- EMET: "he did not appear to his wife but went into the wilderness"
- LOGOS: "withdrew from his wife's presence"
- PNEUMA: "slipped away without going home to his wife"
- Note: Greek *ouk ephanē tē gynaiki autou* = "he did not appear to his wife." EMET is most literal; PNEUMA adds narrative drama ("slipped away").

**8. 1:4 — "prayer shall be my food and drink"**
- EMET/LOGOS: preserve the phrase
- PNEUMA: "Prayer will be the only thing that sustains me"
- Note: The Greek *hē proseuchē mou estai moi brōma kai poma* is more compact. EMET's rendering is closest.
